title: Filioque is hard, but can be proved from Scripture — Rome's own arguments against the Greeks
source_text: XXV. Nonnulli quoque Pontificiorum urgent dogma de processione Spiritus sancti ex Filio, de qua inter Ecclesiam Graecam & Romanam contentio est: Quasi dogma etiam illud ex Scripturis ostendi, & probari nequeat. Sed primo nobis durum valde videtur dogma istud inter ea numerare quae absque salutis jactura negari non possunt. Et quamvis in hac quaestione Ecclesiae Romanae sententiam ut veriorem sequamur, si tamen Ecclesiae Graecae nullum alium errorem haberent, non ideo de salute earum acerum putaremus, neque communionem cum ipsis detrectaremus. Deinde, licet processio illa Spiritus sancti ex Patre & Filio res plane ardua sit, & longe supra captum nostrum, negamus tamen illam ex Scripturis probari non posse. Imo non aliis argumentis illam nobis persuademus, quam quae ex sacra Scriptura duci possunt, ut quod Spiritus sanctus non minus dicitur Spiritus Filii, quam Patris, quod a Filio ut a Patre mittitur, aliaque ejusmodi, quae Theologi nostri ex variis Scripturae locis deducunt & explicant. Quin ipsi Pontificii, dum Graecos dissentientes refellere nituntur, non aliis fere argumentis utuntur quam ex Scriptura ductis, quae plurima congerunt, ut videre est, non tantum apud Petrum Lombardum, sed apud Bessarionem & Bellarminum Cardinales. Ita ut adversarii hic fateri cogantur, vel processionem Spiritus ex Filio per Scripturam probari posse, vel se perperam atque sophistice contra Graecos argumentari.
pass_a_gloss: Some of the Pontiffs also urge the dogma of the procession of the Holy Spirit from the Son, about which there is contention between the Greek and Roman Church: As if that dogma also cannot be shown and proved from the Scriptures. But first it seems very hard to us to number that dogma among those things which cannot be denied without loss of salvation. And although in this question we follow the Roman Church's opinion as the truer, yet if the Greek Churches had no other error, we would not therefore think bitterly of their salvation, nor refuse communion with them. Then, although that procession of the Holy Spirit from the Father and the Son is a plainly arduous matter, and far above our grasp, yet we deny that it cannot be proved from the Scriptures. Indeed we persuade ourselves of it by no other arguments than those which can be drawn from sacred Scripture, as that the Holy Spirit is called no less the Spirit of the Son than of the Father, that He is sent by the Son as by the Father, and other such things, which our theologians deduce and explain from various places of Scripture. Nay the Pontiffs themselves, while they strive to refute the dissenting Greeks, use almost no other arguments than those drawn from Scripture, which they heap up in great number, as may be seen not only in Peter Lombard, but in Cardinals Bessarion and Bellarmine. So that the adversaries are here forced to confess either that the procession of the Spirit from the Son can be proved by Scripture, or that they argue wrongly and sophistically against the Greeks.
pass_b_english: Some also press the Filioque — procession of the Spirit from the Son — as if Scripture cannot show it.
We will not list it among truths that cannot be denied without losing salvation.
We prefer Rome's reading, yet would not damn the Greeks for this alone or break communion over it.
The mystery is hard, but we deny it cannot be proved from Scripture: Spirit of the Son, sent by the Son as by the Father.
Rome herself piles Scripture texts against the Greeks — Lombard, Bessarion, Bellarmine — so she must admit either Scripture proves the Filioque or her anti-Greek case is sophistic.
